issues.text: The one good thing B does is narrow down to an individual ticker, and that is really the only good thing it does. Everything else is disproportionate to the setting. It requires ground truth labels that do not exist here and manufactures them through a consented survey of 500 respondents per country plus provider-revealed seeds - work this desk cannot commission and should not need. The anchor stack behind it (five national regulators, OSM branch tags, published tariff schedules, benefit calendars keyed to national numbering systems) is a standing maintenance burden for a three-person data team, and putting GDPR clearance as gate zero means the project can die before producing anything.
issues.label: blocking
issues.gist: Plan B is disproportionate to the setting: it needs nonexistent ground-truth labels manufactured via an uncommissionable 500-per-country survey, an unmaintainable anchor stack for a three-person team, and a GDPR gate that can kill the project before output
